Segel.et: From Middle High German sëgel, from Old High German sëgal, from Proto-West Germanic *segl. The word was originally masculine in Upper German, while Central German usage varied. The neuter was later reinforced by cognate Middle Low German sēgel, seil n.

Segen.et: From Middle High German segen, from Old High German segan, from Latin signum. Cognate to Low German Siägen (Münsterländisch, Lippisch). Compare English sign.
